item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-bb92cfe914a43ddd","start_unit":1,"end_unit":1,"fact_summary":"A coalition of NGOs submitted a legal analysis concluding that Egyptian authorities’ torture practices were widespread and systematic and amounted to a crime against humanity; it identified beatings, electric shocks, sexual violence, denial of medical care and family contact, and use of torture to suppress dissent.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.5","3B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report was published in October 2023 and describes ongoing and historical practices relevant to the 2023 period.","ruler_attribution":"The analysis attributes the practices to Egyptian authorities and state security institutions under Sisi’s government.","limitations":["The source is an NGO legal analysis rather than a judicial finding."]},{"source_id":"SRC-bb92cfe914a43ddd","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"The report states that torture was enabled by emergency and counter-terrorism laws and by impunity, and that officials at the highest levels knew or should have known of widespread torture against dissenters.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.5","3B.9","7B.2","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The source reports the institutional condition during the 2023 review period.","ruler_attribution":"The finding concerns state policy and senior officials under Sisi’s administration.","limitations":["The source reports the NGO coalition’s assessment and does not establish individual criminal liability."]},{"source_id":"SRC-bb92cfe914a43ddd","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"The report states that the UN Committee against Torture had twice found torture in Egypt widespread and systematic, in 1996 and 2017, and that UN bodies again expressed concern about counter-terrorism legislation targeting human rights defenders in 2021 and 2023.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.5","3B.10","7B.2"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The 2023 UN Human Rights Committee concern is directly within the period; earlier findings provide institutional continuity.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern Egyptian state practices continued under Sisi.","limitations":["The cited unit summarizes prior UN findings without reproducing their full determinations."]},{"source_id":"SRC-bf5ec2d0440984f3","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Amnesty reported that 14 human rights defenders and critics had been arbitrarily detained since 2018, subjected to enforced disappearance, and that 13 detainees were tortured or ill-treated by National Security Agency personnel through beatings, electric shocks, sexual violence, and threats against relatives.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.5","3B.8","3B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The detainees remained detained and on trial during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The conduct is attributed to Egyptian security forces and authorities under Sisi.","limitations":["The source reports Amnesty’s findings and allegations concerning individual cases."]},{"source_id":"SRC-bf5ec2d0440984f3","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Complaints to Supreme State Security Prosecution about disappearance and torture were not adequately investigated; detainees were denied family visits, some lacked adequate healthcare, and the emergency-court proceedings were described as politically motivated.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.5","3B.9","4B.3","4B.9","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The proceedings and detention conditions were current in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The failures concern Egyptian prosecution, prison, and executive authorities.","limitations":["The source is an Amnesty assessment, not a final court ruling."]},{"source_id":"SRC-bf5ec2d0440984f3","start_unit":4,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"The Emergency State Security Court proceedings barred private lawyer communication, restricted access to case files, relied on NSA testimony without adequate cross-examination, held hearings in secret, and provided no ordinary appeal.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.5","4B.4","4B.9","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The trial remained relevant during the 2023 reporting period.","ruler_attribution":"The institutional arrangements were authorized and maintained by Egyptian authorities.","limitations":["The source describes the proceedings through reported statements by lawyers and Amnesty’s investigation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c2b9f2ff8faabaaf","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"The ICJ reported that prisoners at Badr were beaten and placed in solitary confinement after defending an elderly cellmate, and that at least four prisoners had died there since November 2022, with authorities allegedly failing to provide adequate medical assistance in at least three cases.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The incidents and deaths included the 2023 period.","ruler_attribution":"The conduct concerns prison authorities operating under the Egyptian government.","limitations":["The ICJ described allegations and called for an independent investigation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c2b9f2ff8faabaaf","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Human rights organizations reported repeated torture or ill-treatment, arbitrary denial of family contact, inadequate food, water and medical care, harsh lighting, chaining, and suicide attempts at Badr; the authorities had not opened investigations into the deaths or alleged abuse.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.9","3B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The prison conditions and lack of investigations were reported in April 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The finding concerns Egyptian prison authorities and the government’s investigative response.","limitations":["The source aggregates reports from several organizations and does not establish every allegation independently."]},{"source_id":"SRC-06d3f2aa55fe8d26","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"On 5 March 2023, an Emergency State Security Court convicted 30 people in a case involving the Egyptian Coordination for Rights and Freedoms, sentencing 17 to life imprisonment and others to terms of five to 15 years, with five years of police surveillance after release.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The convictions and sentences occurred in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The court and prosecution actions were taken within the executive-controlled emergency-court system under Sisi.","limitations":["The ICJ characterizes the defendants’ activities as lawful human-rights work; the government charged them with terrorism-related offenses."]},{"source_id":"SRC-06d3f2aa55fe8d26","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"The ICJ reported that defendants in the case were subjected to enforced disappearance, torture or ill-treatment, denial of family visits and medical care, interrogation without lawyers, lack of private lawyer access, and no right of appeal; authorities failed to investigate abuse allegations or hold perpetrators accountable.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.5","4B.4","4B.9","7B.2","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The case outcome and continuing detention were reported in March 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The failures concern Egyptian security, prosecution, prison, and emergency-court authorities.","limitations":["The source is an advocacy statement based partly on reported violations."]},{"source_id":"SRC-aea6bdb23bf08112","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"On 15 January 2023, an Emergency State Security Court convicted 82 of 103 defendants in the Joker case, including 23 children at arrest; 38 received life sentences and others received five-, 10-, or 15-year terms, with five years of police surveillance after release.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.7","3B.8","4B.3","4B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The convictions and sentences occurred in January 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The proceedings were conducted by Egyptian emergency courts under Sisi’s government.","limitations":["The ICJ disputes the fairness and rights basis of the convictions."]},{"source_id":"SRC-aea6bdb23bf08112","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The Joker-case defendants, including children, were reportedly subjected to enforced disappearance, prolonged pretrial detention, physical and psychological torture, lawyer restrictions, coerced confessions, and failure by authorities to investigate allegations of abuse.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.5","3B.7","3B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The allegations concerned the case resolved during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The conduct is attributed to Egyptian police, prosecution, courts, and detention authorities.","limitations":["The ICJ relies partly on information from defense lawyers."]},{"source_id":"SRC-79e58a648bec176c","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"CPJ reported that more than 65 percent of journalists imprisoned worldwide in its 2023 census faced anti-state charges such as false news or terrorism; the supplied units do not identify Egypt’s country total.","question_ids":[],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"The census snapshot was taken on 1 December 2023.","ruler_attribution":"No material Egypt-specific attribution is provided in the supplied units.","limitations":["The document’s supplied text does not provide a concrete Egypt-specific fact."]},{"source_id":"SRC-66f1a31202116761","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"In a 1 May 2023 Labor Day speech, Sisi stated that the government had raised the minimum wage, expanded social-protection programs, supported informal workers, sought to integrate people with disabilities and women into employment, expanded national projects for jobs, and prepared a national employment strategy.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.8","6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","8B.1"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The commitments were stated during 2023, but the supplied source does not verify implementation or outcomes.","ruler_attribution":"Directly attributed to President Sisi’s formal speech.","limitations":["The source is a speech report and supports announced policy commitments, not independent performance verification."]},{"source_id":"SRC-66f1a31202116761","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Sisi announced creation of an emergency-assistance fund for informal workers, an immediate 1,000 Egyptian-pound payment for eligible workers outside existing protection programs, a new Aman insurance certificate, enforcement of the statutory five-percent disability employment quota, labor-law dialogue, and a labor-market information platform.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.8","6B.2","6B.3","6B.7","8B.1","8B.2"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"These were announced for implementation in 2023; the supplied source does not establish execution.","ruler_attribution":"Directly attributed to President Sisi’s announced decisions.","limitations":["The source does not provide budget execution, uptake, or independent evaluation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-ca2784ead8739e3a","start_unit":7,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"Sisi won a third presidential term in December 2023 with 89.6 percent of the vote on 66.8 percent turnout; the only potentially serious challenger withdrew after alleging that authorities and pro-regime thugs obstructed endorsements, while 22 campaign members were arrested.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.3","4B.8","4B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The election and reported campaign arrests occurred in December 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The electoral outcome was Sisi’s; allegations concern authorities and pro-regime actors.","limitations":["The electoral commission dismissed the challenger’s allegations."]},{"source_id":"SRC-ca2784ead8739e3a","start_unit":8,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"The report states that dissent had sharply contracted under Sisi, with media and political life brought under security-agency control and thousands arrested, including Islamists, democracy activists, and secular regime critics.","question_ids":["3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","4B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The assessment describes Sisi’s condition at the end of 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Directly attributed to Sisi’s leadership and security agencies.","limitations":["The report provides a broad journalistic assessment rather than a complete arrest dataset."]},{"source_id":"SRC-ca2784ead8739e3a","start_unit":8,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"By December 2023, Egypt faced a severe economic crisis: foreign investors had withdrawn $20 billion from Egyptian debt after Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, the pound had halved against the dollar since March 2022, annual inflation reached almost 35 percent in November, and 60 percent of the population had been in poverty by international definitions before the latest crisis.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.9","5B.10","6B.2","6B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The quantitative indicators describe conditions during 2023 and the preceding baseline.","ruler_attribution":"The report links the crisis partly to extensive foreign borrowing for infrastructure under Sisi, while also identifying the external Ukraine shock.","limitations":["The source does not establish the precise causal contribution of each policy."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e3d0c22b25bf4b6c","start_unit":14,"end_unit":15,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch reported that Egypt heavily restricted civic space during 2023, curtailed expression and peaceful assembly before the presidential vote, and used politically motivated arrests, arbitrary detention, unfair trials, and intimidation to discourage political participation.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.8","4B.1","4B.2","4B.3","4B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report explicitly reviews Egypt during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The conduct is attributed to Sisi’s government.","limitations":["The source is a human-rights organization’s annual assessment."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e3d0c22b25bf4b6c","start_unit":15,"end_unit":16,"fact_summary":"Authorities referred Ahmed Tantawy, his campaign director, and 22 supporters for trial over collecting political endorsements; detained more than 100 actual or perceived supporters; arrested family members; and later convicted or prosecuted other critics on politically motivated charges.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.3","4B.9","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The arrests, referrals, and prosecutions occurred during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The actions are attributed to Egyptian authorities under Sisi.","limitations":["The source characterizes the charges as politically motivated."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e3d0c22b25bf4b6c","start_unit":15,"end_unit":16,"fact_summary":"In 2023, inflation reached 39.7 percent in August; a Bloomberg analysis identified Egypt as the second most vulnerable country to a debt crisis after Ukraine; and HRW reported insufficient increases in social protection and inadequate transparency and civilian oversight of military-owned businesses.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.5","5B.7","5B.9","5B.10","6B.2","6B.5"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The indicators and policy assessment are specific to 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The economic-policy failures are attributed to the Egyptian government under Sisi, with external debt conditions also relevant.","limitations":["The debt-vulnerability result is attributed to a Bloomberg analysis summarized by HRW."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e3d0c22b25bf4b6c","start_unit":16,"end_unit":16,"fact_summary":"The deadline for NGOs to re-register under the 2019 associations law passed in April 2023; HRW states that the law permits authorities to restrict or intervene in independent groups, shut them down, or prosecute their staff.","question_ids":["4B.3","4B.7","4B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The registration deadline and reported effects occurred during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The law and its administration are attributed to Egyptian authorities under Sisi.","limitations":["The supplied text does not identify individual enforcement actions against every NGO."]},{"source_id":"SRC-10409be158f9e777","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"After Sudan’s war began in April 2023, Egypt introduced a visa requirement for all Sudanese nationals; Amnesty reported that approximately 500,000 Sudanese refugees fled to Egypt and that UNHCR estimated 3,000 people were deported to Sudan from Egypt in September 2023 alone.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.9","6B.3","6B.6","6B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The visa change, refugee influx, and September 2023 deportation estimate fall within the period.","ruler_attribution":"The policy is attributed to the Egyptian government; deportations involved border and interior authorities.","limitations":["The source was published in 2024 and reports retrospective estimates."]},{"source_id":"SRC-10409be158f9e777","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Amnesty documented arbitrary arrests and detention of Sudanese refugees, including arrests by police and Border Guard Forces, detention in overcrowded and unsanitary facilities, denial of healthcare, and forced returns without asylum procedures or individualized risk assessment; it estimated that about 800 detainees were forcibly returned between January and March 2024 following the 2023 escalation.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.9","6B.3","6B.6","6B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The mass-arrest campaign began in 2023; the estimated 2024 returns are included as a continuation beyond the target year.","ruler_attribution":"The conduct is attributed to Egyptian police and Border Guard Forces under the Ministries of Interior and Defence.","limitations":["Only the initiation and escalation of the campaign fall within 2023; the main forced-return estimate is for 2024."]},{"source_id":"SRC-4148d8bb6dd8278a","start_unit":8,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"EFHR reported that Egyptian courts issued at least 348 death sentences in 2023, including 16 people in political cases; the Court of Cassation upheld at least 27 death sentences, including three in a political case; and authorities executed at least eight people in criminal cases.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.5","3B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"All figures concern 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern Egyptian courts and authorities under Sisi.","limitations":["EFHR compiled the figures from media monitoring and communications with families and lawyers."]},{"source_id":"SRC-4148d8bb6dd8278a","start_unit":8,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"EFHR reported that Egyptian authorities continued using the death penalty in political-violence cases despite fair-trial concerns, and that Egyptian law allowed capital punishment for 105 offenses across several statutes.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.5","4B.4","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The assessment concerns the 2023 death-penalty system.","ruler_attribution":"The statutory and judicial practices concern the Egyptian state under Sisi.","limitations":["The source is an NGO monitoring report and does not independently adjudicate each case."]},{"source_id":"SRC-6e57b07c956d77d5","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The ICJ reported that enforced disappearance was used systematically against human-rights defenders, lawyers, activists, politicians, and dissidents to create fear and silence criticism; since May 2020 Egypt had received more UN Working Group communications on disappearances than any other country.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.5","3B.8","3B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report was issued in August 2023 and describes an ongoing practice relevant to the period.","ruler_attribution":"The practice is attributed to Egyptian authorities and the National Security Agency under Sisi.","limitations":["The source summarizes UN communications and civil-society documentation rather than a completed international investigation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-6e57b07c956d77d5","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"The Egyptian Commission for Rights and Freedoms documented 3,088 enforced disappearances over seven years from NSA and other official or unofficial detention sites; the ICJ stated that the practice facilitated arbitrary detention, torture, and possible extrajudicial killings, while prosecution investigations in a prominent death-in-custody case failed to establish the circumstances.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.10","7B.2"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The seven-year count and institutional assessment were current through 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The documented sites and investigative failures concern Egyptian state institutions under Sisi.","limitations":["The count is from a civil-society campaign and includes years before 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-6e57b07c956d77d5","start_unit":4,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"Egyptian anti-terrorism law allowed incommunicado detention for up to 28 days at prosecutorial discretion; the ICJ stated that this effectively codified enforced disappearance, and described the unregulated practice of recycling detainees into new cases to prolong detention after release orders.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.5","4B.4","4B.9","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The legal framework and practices were in force and reported in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The law and detention practices were maintained by Egyptian state authorities under Sisi.","limitations":["The ICJ’s characterization is an expert legal assessment, not a domestic court ruling."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-79e58a648bec176c"],"batch_limitations":["The supplied materials are predominantly advocacy and media reports; no scoring is performed.","Several sources report historical or continuing practices whose relevance to 2023 is contextual rather than limited exclusively to that calendar year.","The supplied CPJ document contains no concrete Egypt-specific fact in the provided units."]}
